The '''Royal Language Decree of 1652''' was a language and script standardization decree of the [[Vesperan Kingdom]]. It established a standardized form of the [[Vesperan Language]] for government, law, court use, and formal recordkeeping.

== Background ==

The decree followed the kingdom's consolidation in 1650. The new state needed a reliable administrative language that could be used by courts, royal offices, legal records, and provincial officials.

Earlier western scribal traditions and the [[Royal Scriptorial Decree]] had already created a written foundation. The 1652 decree connected that older script tradition to a more centralized kingdom government.

== Provisions ==

Source material says the decree standardized Classical Vesperan and codified the [[Vesperan Alphabet]] into formal and cursive variants. It gave royal authority to spelling, court vocabulary, legal phrasing, and official recordkeeping.

The decree helped make Vesperan a state language rather than only the language of the ruling region.

== Legacy ==

The decree became one of the main foundations for later imperial language policy. After the [[Imperial Proclamation of 1710]], the [[Imperial Language Academy]] used the older royal standard as the base for imperial grammar, administrative terminology, and script reform.
